newsitem.title: USA: US new corp debt activity seen stirring cautiously.
newsitem.headline: US new corp debt activity seen stirring cautiously.

text.p: Activity is beginning to stir in the corporate bond new issue sector with an ever growing list of new deals expected to come to market, but dealers said issuers may opt to stay put for a while as they size up the rate environment.
"The (U.S.) government market has been beaten up these past few days...there's not a very good tone in the market right now," said one high-grade syndicate source.

A sharp rise in U.S. Treasury yields spurred by stronger-than-expected ecnomic news has kept issuers on the sidelines as they contemplate whether to finance debt at current levels or wait for last year's favorable rate picture to reemerge.

Currently the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is trading up 7/32 at 97-5/32 to yield 6.72 percent. On December 30 the long bond ended the trading day at 6.54 percent, but the yield has steadily risen since.
Meanwhile, US West Capital Funding Inc, a unit of US West Inc, is expected to issue $2.0 billion in a four-part debt offering consisting of five, 10, 30 and 40-year maturities.
"The roadshow (US West Capital) kicks off on Monday...it looks like the deal will price by the end of next week," one syndicate source said.
The deal is expected to be be underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co and is rated A2/BBB-plus, sources said.
Also, Tosco Corp is expected to tap the market midweek with a $600 million three-part debt offering via Morgan Stanley & Co, sources said.
The Tosco deal is expected to consist of $200 million in 10-year debt, $300 million in 30-year debt and $100 million in 50-year debt, sources added.
Among other names circulating the market are Aon Corp's expected $700 million deal consisting of 30-year trust preferred securities via Morgan Stanley, dealers said.
In addition, TCI Communications Inc's is expected to issue a $500 million trust preferreds deal via Lehman Brothers, dealers added.

Turning to the high-yield sector, Tenet Healthcare is getting set to bring a two-part debt offering consisting of $800 million in notes due 2005 and $500 million in notes due 2007, market sources said.
The deal is expected to be underwritten by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
Also, Multicanal SA, an Argentinian cable company, is expected to sell $250 million in junk bonds via a 144A private debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.
Orion Network Systems is expected to bring a two-part deal consisting of $222 million in senior notes due 2007 and $100 million in senior discount notes, via Morgan Stanely.

Other junk bond issuers expected to tap the market in the coming month are Systems International, Corning Clinical Labs, Bresnan Communications, ACF Industries, Syratech Corp, Pocket Communications and Premier Parks, high-yield sources said.
New zero coupon bond deals are also expected to reappear in early 1997 after having faded for several months.

Issuers include Optelcom, which is expected to issue $150 million in zeros, General Wireless which is preparing a $220 million deal and UIH Australia/Pacific Inc which is expected to issue a $150 million zero coupon issue, dealers added.
Among foreign issuers, Argentina is rumored to bring a mega global debt offering of between $2.0 and $3.0 billion in late January via Merrill Lynch & Co, syndicate sources said.
Argentina's debt offering is expected to consist of longer-dated maturities, sources said.
Italy is also expected to issue $1.0 billion in 10-year global debt in early January, sources said.
State Development Bank of China is said to also be preparing a deal of its own consisting of $300 million in 10-year yankee debt, syndicate sources said.
In addition, Columbia, Finland and Israel are rumored to bring debt deals of their own near-term, they added.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
